pair.topic_type: post-cutoff civil-disobedience movement vs interim government

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The sole demand of the 2024 non-cooperation movement was the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The sole demand of this movement was the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her cabinet.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Asif Mahmud was one of the coordinators of the 2024 non-cooperation movement.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On the morning of 3 August, one of the movement coordinators, Asif Mahmud, stated in a Facebook post that they would start a "non-cooperation movement" against the government

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Nahid Islam addressed the assembled crowd at Shaheed Minar to announce the movement's exclusive demand.
knowledge_cards.source_span: At around 5:30 p.m., Nahid Islam, one of the coordinators, addressed the assembled crowd at Shaheed Minar and announced that the movement's exclusive demand was the resignation of Hasina and her cabinet.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: President Mohammed Shahabuddin announced the formation of an Interim government following Sheikh Hasina's removal.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Widespread celebrations and violence occurred following her removal, while the military and President Mohammed Shahabuddin announced the formation of an Interim government

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Interim government formed after the 2024 non-cooperation movement was led by Muhammad Yunus.
knowledge_cards.source_span: the military and President Mohammed Shahabuddin announced the formation of an Interim government led by Muhammad Yunus.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Chief of Army Staff Waker-uz-Zaman convened a meeting to call for the creation of an interim government.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 5 August, the Chief of Army Staff, Waker-uz-Zaman, convened a meeting with representatives from BNP, Jatiya Party (Ershad), and Jamaat-e-Islami and called for the creation of an interim government

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sajeeb Wazed is the son of Sheikh Hasina.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Hasina's son, Sajeeb Wazed, later said that his mother had begun considering resignation as early as 3 August

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Ajit Doval, the Indian National Security Advisor, reportedly received Sheikh Hasina at the Hindan Air Force Station.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Shortly, she was reported to have landed at the Hindan Air Force Station in Ghaziabad, on the outskirts of the Indian capital New Delhi, and was reportedly received by the Indian National Security Advisor, Ajit Doval at the base.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Students Against Discrimination announced a one-point demand for the resignation of the Prime Minister.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 3 August 2024, coordinators of the Students Against Discrimination announced a one-point demand for the resignation of the Prime Minister and her cabinet

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The 2024 non-cooperation movement was a mass uprising against the Awami League-led government.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The non-cooperation movement, also known as the one-point movement, was a disinvestment movement and a mass uprising against the Awami League-led government of Bangladesh

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Bangladesh Police issued an official statement regarding the attacks on police facilities during the movement.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Twenty-seven police facilities were attacked and vandalized, and a hundred policemen were injured in these incidents, according to an official statement by the Bangladesh Police.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) was directed to remain in barracks and coastal areas during the non-cooperation movement.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Forces other than the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and the Navy will not perform duty outside the cantonment. The BGB and the Navy will remain in barracks and coastal areas.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) dismissed the head of its Bauphal upazila branch following complaints of involvement in violence.
knowledge_cards.section_title: Reprisal attacks against Awami League supporters and police
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 10 August, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) dismissed the head of its Bauphal upazila branch following complaints about his alleged involvement in the violence and looting.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Representatives from Jamaat-e-Islami attended a meeting convened by the Chief of Army Staff to discuss the creation of an interim government.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 5 August, the Chief of Army Staff, Waker-uz-Zaman, convened a meeting with representatives from BNP, Jatiya Party (Ershad), and Jamaat-e-Islami and called for the creation of an interim government

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Storming of Ganabhaban occurred when protesters entered the Prime Minister's residence.
knowledge_cards.source_span: === Storming of Ganabhaban === Shortly after Sheikh Hasina's departure, at around 3:00 p.m., protesters reached the gates of the Ganabhaban and entered the Prime Minister's residence

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Long March to Dhaka was organized by protesters to force Sheikh Hasina out of power.
knowledge_cards.source_span: === Long March to Dhaka === Asif Mahmud, a coordinator of the Students Against Discrimination, announced that their march to Dhaka had been rescheduled to 5 August

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Arrest of Awami League leaders took place as several figures associated with the administration attempted to flee Bangladesh.
knowledge_cards.source_span: === Arrest of Awami League leaders === In addition to Sheikh Hasina, several figures associated with her administration and the Awami League fled or attempted to flee Bangladesh.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: On 3 August 2024, coordinators of the Students Against Discrimination announced a one-point demand for the resignation of the Prime Minister.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 3 August 2024, coordinators of the Students Against Discrimination announced a one-point demand for the resignation of the Prime Minister and her cabinet

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: On 4 August, thousands of protesters gathered at the Shahbagh intersection as a form of civil disobedience.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 4 August, thousands of protesters gathered at the Shahbagh intersection in the morning, obstructing it as a form of civil disobedience to demand the government's resignation.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: On 5 August 2024, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled the country.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 5 August 2024, at around 3:00 p.m., Prime Minister Hasina resigned and fled the country on a helicopter

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The curfew imposed during the non-cooperation movement was rescinded on 6 August.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The curfew was rescinded on 6 August, and offices, businesses, and schools were permitted to resume operations on the same day.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Muhammad Yunus returned to Dhaka and was inaugurated as the head of the interim government on 8 August.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Yunus, who was in Paris, returned to Dhaka on 8 August and was inaugurated later that day along with the rest of his cabinet at the Bangabhaban.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The coordinators called for a long march to Dhaka to force Hasina out of power.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The coordinators called for a long march to Dhaka to force Hasina out of power on 5 August.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Protesters reached the gates of the Ganabhaban and entered the Prime Minister's residence.
knowledge_cards.source_span: protesters reached the gates of the Ganabhaban and entered the Prime Minister's residence looting, vandalizing, and destroying numerous items

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Thousands of protesters gathered at the Shahbagh intersection to demand the government's resignation.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 4 August, thousands of protesters gathered at the Shahbagh intersection in the morning, obstructing it as a form of civil disobedience

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sheikh Hasina arrived in Delhi via Agartala after fleeing Bangladesh.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Prime Minister Hasina resigned and fled the country on a helicopter with her sister, Sheikh Rehana, to India, arriving in Delhi via Agartala.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sheikh Hasina was reported to have landed at the Hindan Air Force Station in Ghaziabad.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Shortly, she was reported to have landed at the Hindan Air Force Station in Ghaziabad, on the outskirts of the Indian capital New Delhi

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled to India.
knowledge_cards.source_span: At around 3:00 p.m. (UTC+6), Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled to India, her government's biggest ally.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sheikh Hasina was expected to seek political asylum in the United Kingdom.
knowledge_cards.source_span: She is expected to proceed to London for her safe passage and seek political asylum in the United Kingdom

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: A United Nations (UN) team arrived in Bangladesh to discuss human rights.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 22 August, a United Nations (UN) team arrived in Bangladesh to discuss and understand the interim government's priorities for promoting human rights.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Muhammad Yunus was sworn in as the Chief Adviser of Bangladesh.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The leadership of Muhammad Yunus began on 8 August 2024 when he was sworn in as the Chief Adviser of Bangladesh

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: President Mohammed Shahabuddin administered the oath ceremony for Muhammad Yunus.
knowledge_cards.source_span: President of Bangladesh Mohammed Shahabuddin administered the oath ceremony.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: General Waker-uz-Zaman handed the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to the President.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 5 August 2024, General Waker-uz-Zaman, the Chief of the Army Staff, handed the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to President Mohammed Shahabuddin

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Sheikh Hasina resigned as prime minister and departed to India.
knowledge_cards.source_span: In August 2024, after the Resignation of Sheikh Hasina as prime minister and her departure to India following the July Uprising

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Asif Nazrul served as the law, justice and parliamentary affairs adviser to the interim government.
knowledge_cards.source_span: However, the law, justice and parliamentary affairs adviser to the government, Asif Nazrul, said that the incumbent would "remain in power as long as necessary".

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Economist Debapriya Bhattacharya was appointed to head a committee charged with drafting a white paper on the economy of Bangladesh.
knowledge_cards.source_span: In August 2024, the Yunus administration appointed economist Debapriya Bhattacharya to head a committee charged with drafting a white paper on the economy of Bangladesh.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Muhammad Yunus sent a personal letter to President Donald Trump urging him to reconsider tariffs.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 7 April, Yunus sent a personal letter to President Donald Trump urging to reconsider the tariffs and requested a three-month postponement of the decision

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed full support for Bangladesh's interim government.
knowledge_cards.source_span: During the visit, Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed full support for Bangladesh's interim government and pledged to expand economic and technical cooperation.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Muhammad Yunus and Narendra Modi met each other for the first time since the ouster of Hasina.
knowledge_cards.source_span: On 4 April 2025, Yunus and Modi met each other for the first time since the ouster of Hasina in August 2024.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The key coordinators of the Students Against Discrimination announced that Yunus would be Chief Adviser.
knowledge_cards.source_span: the key coordinators of the Students Against Discrimination announced that Yunus would be Chief Adviser of the Interim government of Bangladesh.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) reported that substantial challenges persist in areas such as politics and the economy.
knowledge_cards.source_span: While the interim government initiated significant reform measures, substantial challenges persist in areas such as politics, the economy, and institutional accountability as reported by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB).

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The Yunus government lifted the ban on Jamaat-e-Islami.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The Yunus government also lifted the ban on the Jamaat-e-Islami as an organization that had been placed by the Hasina government

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The interim government banned the Awami League as an organization under the anti-terrorism act.
knowledge_cards.source_span: the government banned the Awami League as an organization under the anti-terrorism act.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The National Citizen Party held a massive demonstration before the banning of the Awami League.
knowledge_cards.source_span: In April 2025, after a massive demonstration by the National Citizen Party, citizens & other political parties like the Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, the government banned the Awami League

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh participated in demonstrations alongside the National Citizen Party.

knowledge_cards.source_span: In the banking sector the government reorganized the Board of Directors of Bangladesh Bank (BB)

knowledge_cards.source_span: In February 2025, following a widespread outburst of violence in the aftermath of Demolition of Dhanmondi 32, the administration launched Operation Devil Hunt to quell the violence.

knowledge_cards.source_span: This was followed by the dissolvement of the parliament on 6 August 2024 by the President, Mohammed Shahabuddin.

knowledge_cards.source_span: On 10 August 2024, he also visited the home and family members of Abu Sayed and paid respects to Sayed's grave in Rangpur.

knowledge_cards.source_span: On 13 August, he visited the Dhakeshwari National Temple, the main place of worship for the Hindu minority in the capital city of Dhaka

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: Muhammad Yunus and Narendra Modi engaged in a bilateral meeting in Bangkok.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Both leaders engaged in a bilateral meeting in the sideline of 6th BIMSTEC summit in Bangkok.
